documents.name: Aletsch Glacier Trail: Moosfluh–Märjelensee–Fiescheralp
documents.summary: A sustained close-range traverse above the Great Aletsch Glacier through moraine, rock steps and Märjelensee.
documents.whyWorthwhile: One of Switzerland’s strongest non-glacial ways to experience the scale and changing margin of the Aletsch landscape for hours rather than from a lift viewpoint.

documents.name: Greina crossing via Terrihütte
documents.summary: A two-day crossing of the broad, river-cut Greina high plateau, a protected tundra-like landscape unlike Switzerland’s sharper postcard Alps.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Greina’s scale, remoteness and water-shaped plateau are difficult to substitute elsewhere, and the crossing reveals it far better than a quick out-and-back.

documents.name: Hohtürli: Griesalp–Oeschinensee–Kandersteg
documents.summary: A complete high-pass crossing beneath Blüemlisalp ice, climbing the dramatic Hohtürli stair system before descending to Oeschinensee and Kandersteg.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The pass, glacier scenery and Oeschinensee finale form a much stronger destination hike than treating the lake as a standalone outing.

coverImage.alt: Documentary photograph of Hohtürli Pass, representative of Hohtürli: Griesalp–Oeschinensee–Kandersteg.

documents.name: Lais da Macun: Zernez–Munt Baselgia–Lavin
documents.summary: A demanding rail-to-rail high route over Munt Baselgia into the crystalline Macun lake plateau and down to Lavin.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Repeated independent full-route reports and a national once-in-a-lifetime hiking shortlist support Macun as an itinerary-changing Swiss mountain hike: the complete journey sustains exceptional scenery and variety rather than relying on one viewpoint.

legacy-best-season.label: Best season
legacy-best-season.note: The official route season is July through October, subject to current trail status, a favourable forecast and suitable snow-free conditions.

legacy-access-point.label: Access point
legacy-access-point.note: The native route begins and ends on the public footway at the respective railway stations; the full recommended variant is rail-to-rail.

documents.name: Schynige Platte–Faulhorn–First
documents.summary: A long panorama traverse linking Schynige Platte, Faulhorn and Bachalpsee with sustained views of Lakes Thun and Brienz and the Eiger–Mönch–Jungfrau skyline.
documents.whyWorthwhile: It sustains exceptional scenery for most of the day and turns several famous viewpoints into one coherent high-level journey.

documents.name: Segnespass and Segnesboden traverse
documents.summary: A high crossing through the UNESCO Sardona tectonic landscape combining Martinsloch, pale erosion basins and both Segnes plateaus.
documents.whyWorthwhile: One of Switzerland’s strongest geology-led hikes: it crosses the tectonic landscape rather than merely viewing it from Flims.

documents.name: Swiss Science Center Technorama
documents.summary: Swiss Science Center Technorama is a science discovery destination in Winterthur, retained for distinctive visitor-experience quality.
documents.whyWorthwhile: One of Europe’s strongest experiment-led science centres, with extraordinary density of robust hands-on phenomena.

audience.notes: Editorial destination-fit profile derived from the researched positive age span. Bands without positive evidence remain unknown rather than being treated as a positive match or a hard prohibition. Individual rides and activities may have stricter operator rules.

coverImage.alt: Swiss Science Center Technorama visitor environment

documents.name: Three classic passes — Grimsel, Furka & Susten
documents.summary: A 131 km Swiss alpine loop from Meiringen linking the Grimsel, Furka and Susten passes in one continuous high-mountain circuit.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The route combines three major Swiss passes into one coherent circuit, moving through lake-and-waterfall country, glacier-facing high alpine terrain and long engineered mountain-road descents without requiring three separate out-and-back detours.

coverImage.alt: The Furka Pass road descending through high alpine terrain as seen from the Grimsel side.

documents.name: Aareschlucht
documents.summary: A 1.4 km engineered passage through the narrow Aare gorge between Meiringen and Innertkirchen.
documents.whyWorthwhile: One of Switzerland's strongest accessible gorge walks: sustained, dramatic and easy to execute.

documents.name: Bellinzona
documents.summary: A compact Ticino city where a lived-in old centre sits inside one of Switzerland's strongest urban fortress landscapes.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Independent 2026 destination-level evidence supports Bellinzona itself as a meaningful Swiss detour, especially in the complete main-season castle period.

booking.note: Ordinary city and castle visits do not generally require advance booking.

coreExperience.note: Italian is local; the old-town and fortress experience is primarily visual.
English official fortress information is available.

mobility.note: Walking the three-castle system entails meaningful climbing; transit can reduce it.

legacy-effort-required.label: Effort required
legacy-effort-required.note: Moderate if all three castles are walked; bus and tourist-train options can reduce climbing.

documents.name: CERN Science Gateway
documents.summary: CERN Science Gateway is a science discovery destination in Meyrin, retained for distinctive visitor-experience quality.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A major interactive particle-physics visitor centre that makes a normally inaccessible research institution tangible.

audience.notes: Editorial destination-fit profile derived from the researched positive age span. Bands without positive evidence remain unknown rather than being treated as a positive match or a hard prohibition. Individual rides and activities may have stricter operator rules.

documents.name: Chaplin’s World
documents.summary: Chaplin’s World is a immersive biographical destination in Corsier-sur-Vevey, retained for distinctive visitor-experience quality.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A carefully staged studio-and-home experience that turns biography and film history into immersive sets rather than static display cases.

audience.notes: Editorial destination-fit profile derived from the researched positive age span. Bands without positive evidence remain unknown rather than being treated as a positive match or a hard prohibition. Individual rides and activities may have stricter operator rules.

documents.name: Corbassière bridge and Cabane Panossière
documents.localName: Cabane Brunet – Passerelle de Corbassière – Panossière
documents.summary: A close glacier-cirque hike to the 190 m Corbassière suspension bridge and Cabane Panossière beneath the Grand Combin massif.
documents.whyWorthwhile: It provides a dramatic glacier environment and bridge experience without the fixed-rope terrain required by several rival glacier-hut approaches.

variants.name: Cabane Brunet to Cabane Panossière return

documents.name: Creux du Van circuit
documents.summary: A full ascent and circuit of the monumental semicircular Creux du Van limestone amphitheatre rather than a drive-up rim viewpoint.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The full circuit makes the cliff’s scale legible and is the strongest destination-level Jura hike found without entering technical terrain.

documents.name: Jungfraujoch – Top of Europe
documents.summary: The high-altitude railway visitor complex at Jungfraujoch, combining glacier access, panoramic platforms and indoor attractions.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A genuinely destination-worthy rail-to-glacier experience, but current price, crowd and weather evidence prevents an automatic S rating.

documents.name: Lai da Rims from Prà da Vau
documents.localName: Prà da Vau – Lai da Rims
documents.summary: A quiet high-alpine circuit to the intensely turquoise Lai da Rims above Val Müstair, using a higher start to avoid poor-value road kilometres.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The lake’s colour and austere setting are unusually strong, and the Prà da Vau start concentrates the day on the exceptional upper landscape.

documents.name: Lapis de Zanfleuron
documents.summary: An otherworldly traverse across recently deglaciated limestone, older deeply dissolved karst, moraines, fissures and dolines near Sanetsch.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Few nontechnical Swiss hikes provide such direct evidence of glacial retreat and karst development in one compact landscape.

documents.name: Lötschenpass: Lauchernalp–Selden
documents.summary: A historic trans-Alpine pass crossing through moraine, glacial debris and old mule-route terrain into the wild Gasterntal.
documents.whyWorthwhile: History, glacier-shaped terrain and a genuine valley-to-valley crossing give it much more character than a conventional high viewpoint hike.

documents.name: Monte Tamaro–Monte Lema traverse
documents.summary: A long open southern-Alpine ridge traverse with Lake Maggiore, Lake Lugano and the higher Alps unfolding around the central crest.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The Mediterranean-Alpine character and sustained ridge journey are substantially more distinctive than a simple Monte Tamaro summit outing.

documents.name: Murgseen loop
documents.summary: A lift-free circuit through three mountain lakes, waterfalls, old Swiss stone-pine forest and a compact glacial basin above Murgtal.
documents.whyWorthwhile: It offers a quieter, less engineered lake experience than Pizol while remaining consistently scenic enough to justify a substantial detour.

documents.name: Obersteinberg and Oberhornsee
documents.summary: A hard lift-free ascent into the remote waterfall-and-glacier amphitheatre behind Lauterbrunnen, continuing beyond Obersteinberg to Oberhornsee.
documents.whyWorthwhile: It reveals the wild upper landscape hidden behind the famous valley floor and offers much more solitude and route substance than the roadside waterfall circuit.

documents.name: Pizol Five Lakes hike
documents.summary: Five strongly contrasting alpine lakes threaded through a succession of glacial cirques, with high route quality between the headline viewpoints.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The density and visual variation of the lake sequence make this more than a photogenic stop and one of Switzerland’s strongest lift-assisted full-day hikes.

documents.name: Rhine Falls
documents.summary: A broad, high-volume Rhine waterfall with close viewing platforms and seasonal boat approaches.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A major, repeatably impressive European waterfall whose scale and close access justify a dedicated detour.

documents.name: Rigi Kulm
documents.summary: A cogwheel-accessed 1,798 m summit viewpoint with a broad panorama over Central Switzerland.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A genuinely detour-worthy summit panorama with unusually low access friction, provided the weather is clear.

documents.name: Silberen karst loop
documents.summary: A hard circuit onto the enormous Silberen limestone pavement, a maze of fissures, sinkholes and sculpted pale rock above the Hölloch cave system.
documents.whyWorthwhile: One of Switzerland’s most unusual walkable geological landscapes, with very high discovery value despite awkward road access.

documents.name: Stoos ridge: Klingenstock–Fronalpstock
documents.summary: A compact engineered ridge above Lake Lucerne with an almost continuous panorama between Klingenstock and Fronalpstock.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The scenery-to-effort ratio is exceptional and delivers genuine ridge character without requiring exposed scrambling.

documents.name: Swiss Museum of Transport
documents.summary: Swiss Museum of Transport is a transport discovery destination in Lucerne, retained for distinctive visitor-experience quality.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A huge transport and technology destination with simulators, interactive exhibits and enough breadth for a full day.

audience.notes: Editorial destination-fit profile derived from the researched positive age span. Bands without positive evidence remain unknown rather than being treated as a positive match or a hard prohibition. Individual rides and activities may have stricter operator rules.

coverImage.alt: Swiss Museum of Transport visitor environment

documents.name: Tour des Gastlosen
documents.summary: A full circuit around the serrated Gastlosen limestone wall, continually changing the shape, scale and light on one of the western Prealps’ most distinctive rock formations.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The circuit is consistently rewarding rather than a single viewpoint and has unusually strong rock architecture for a nontechnical Prealpine hike.

documents.name: Trümmelbach Falls
documents.summary: Ten glacier-fed waterfalls channelled through galleries inside the Lauterbrunnen valley wall.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A rare, powerful and hard-to-substitute waterfall experience that justifies a meaningful Lauterbrunnen detour.

documents.name: Val Calnègia from Foroglio
documents.summary: A steep historic path above Foroglio into a hanging side valley of waterfalls, stone bridges, boulder shelters and preserved seasonal settlements.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Most visitors stop at Foroglio waterfall; continuing into Calnègia reveals the exceptional human-landscape adaptation that makes Val Bavona destination-worthy.

coverImage.alt: Documentary photograph of Waterfall at Foroglio, representative of Val Calnègia from Foroglio.

documents.name: Val Trupchun loop
documents.summary: A nontechnical wildlife-focused hike deep into a strictly protected Swiss National Park valley, especially strong for marmots, red deer, chamois and ibex.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Few Swiss routes combine this level of intact habitat, wildlife opportunity and low technical risk; the valley itself is the attraction rather than a summit viewpoint.

documents.name: VerticAlp Emosson
documents.summary: A three-stage mountain railway journey from Le Châtelard to Émosson using a steep funicular, panoramic train and Minifunic.
documents.whyWorthwhile: An unusually coherent mountain-transport experience whose journey itself repeatedly earns destination-level praise.

documents.name: Vieux Emosson geological loop
documents.summary: A geology-rich loop linking two major dams, glacially polished rock, the Veudale gorge and a high Triassic tracksite now understood to preserve chirotheriid archosaur/reptile footprints rather than dinosaur tracks.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Deep-time geology, visible fossil tracks and giant human infrastructure form a route unlike a generic alpine lake walk.

documents.name: Zoo Zürich
documents.summary: One of Europe's strongest modern zoos, led by exceptionally immersive Masoala rainforest and Lewa savannah habitats despite significant current redevelopment.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The zoo is strong enough to justify a meaningful Zürich detour for zoo and habitat-design enthusiasts, but current construction keeps it below S.

booking.note: Advance online tickets reduce arrival friction but ordinary admission is not generally capacity-booked.

coreExperience.note: Animal and habitat experience is primarily visual; English visitor information is available.

mobility.note: A complete visit covers a large, hilly site and normally takes several hours.

current.note: The zoo is operating, but redevelopment keeps the former Pantanal area unavailable during aviary construction through 2028.

documents.name: Zürich Opera House
documents.summary: A consistently high-level European opera house whose strongest casts, orchestra and conducting justify planning a performance into a Zürich stay.
documents.whyWorthwhile: For opera and ballet audiences, current performance evidence is strong enough to justify an A-tier detour; it is the programmed performance, not simply the façade, that earns the rating.

booking.note: Popular casts and productions can sell strongly; advance seat choice also matters for surtitles sightlines.

coreExperience.note: Most operas are performed in original language; understanding German or English surtitles materially improves narrative comprehension.
German and English surtitles are provided for almost all operas, though visibility depends on seat.

mobility.note: Normal seated performance visit; accessibility depends on assigned seating and venue route.

legacy-booking-advice.label: Booking advice
legacy-booking-advice.note: Advance booking is recommended for sought productions; choose seats with surtitles visibility if relying on English text.

legacy-accessibility-notes.label: Accessibility
legacy-accessibility-notes.note: Check production and seat-specific accessibility before purchase.

documents.name: Areuse Gorge: Noiraigue–Boudry
documents.summary: A consistently attractive rail-to-rail descent through the Areuse Gorge with river narrows, stone steps, bridges and forest.
documents.whyWorthwhile: One of the Jura’s best sustained gorge walks and unusually easy to execute by public transport, though less destination-shaping than Creux du Van.

documents.name: B&B Gästehaus Rössli Schwellbrunn
documents.summary: A small, highly praised village guesthouse whose warm hosting, breakfast and Appenzell setting make the stay part of the trip rather than generic lodging.
documents.whyWorthwhile: For travellers deliberately staying in the Appenzell countryside, the guesthouse has enough recurring experience quality to be a clearly worthwhile B-tier accommodation choice.

visualSignals.label: Experience
visualSignals.value: Appenzell village guesthouse stay · historic bed-and-breakfast

booking.note: Small inventory makes advance reservation sensible.

coreExperience.note: German is local; international guest evidence supports practical use by foreign visitors.

mobility.note: Step-free and wheelchair suitability could not be verified from a current operator source; contact the property before booking.

documents.name: Batöni waterfall arena
documents.summary: A compact valley hike to a secluded rock amphitheatre where several major waterfalls converge around Batöni.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The concentrated waterfall geometry is genuinely distinctive and far less internationally visible than Switzerland’s famous waterfall valleys.

documents.name: Brecca–Euschels: Schwarzsee–Jaun
documents.summary: A point-to-point crossing through the Breccaschlund karst cirque and old pasture landscape before crossing toward Jaun.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Karst, pasture history and traverse logistics give it more character than an ordinary Prealpine walk, although Gastlosen is the stronger rock spectacle.

coverImage.alt: Documentary photograph of Breccaschlund 02, representative of Brecca–Euschels: Schwarzsee–Jaun.

documents.name: Breggia Gorge Park geological walk
documents.summary: A compact geological and industrial-heritage walk through a gorge exposing roughly 200 million years of rock history beside former quarries and cement infrastructure.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The collision of deep-time geology, river gorge and industrial archaeology is unusually distinctive for such a compact low-altitude walk.

documents.name: Chapel Bridge
documents.summary: Lucerne's covered timber bridge is a short but unusually atmospheric crossing, with historic painted panels, river views and the Water Tower composing a defining urban landmark.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The bridge is genuinely worthwhile and repeatedly praised, but the core experience is too brief and context-dependent to justify A-level tiering by itself.

coreExperience.note: The core bridge and painted-panel experience is primarily visual.

mobility.note: The public pedestrian crossing is wheelchair-accessible according to Lucerne visitor information.

documents.name: District 1
documents.summary: Zürich's District 1 forms a coherent historic city-centre experience on both sides of the Limmat rather than just a loose collection of famous pins.
documents.whyWorthwhile: For a Zürich visit, District 1 is a clearly worthwhile urban destination layer, though compact scale and tourist-commercial pressure keep it at B rather than A.

booking.note: The district itself requires no booking.

coreExperience.note: German is local; the street-and-architecture experience is not language-dependent.

mobility.note: Pedestrian-friendly, but some historic streets are cobbled and building accessibility varies.

legacy-effort-required.label: Effort required
legacy-effort-required.note: Low to moderate urban walking; the useful core is pedestrian and transit-rich.

documents.name: Erlebnisberg Pradaschier
documents.summary: A lift-served mountain activity area above Churwalden anchored by a long toboggan run.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A strong regional mountain-play destination with enough activity density to justify a detour for the right audience.

documents.name: Fräkigaudi Summer Toboggan
documents.summary: A 1,350 m summer toboggan on Fräkmüntegg, marketed as Switzerland's longest summer toboggan run.
documents.whyWorthwhile: One of the few exact sub-attractions in the intake with repeated independent trip-highlight and repeat-ride evidence.

documents.name: Gelmerbahn
documents.summary: An exposed mountain funicular climbing from Handegg toward Gelmersee at a maximum gradient of 106%.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A distinctive mountain-transport thrill with a high-alpine payoff, worth a detour when tickets fit the itinerary.

documents.name: Glacier Canyon Grindelwald
documents.summary: A built walkway into Grindelwald's glacier-cut gorge, including a suspended net above the Lütschine.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A compact, distinctive and reliably enjoyable Grindelwald gorge experience, especially as part of a wider day.

documents.name: God da Tamangur: S-charl–Lü
documents.summary: A quiet traverse through exceptionally high-elevation Swiss stone-pine forest and a cultural mountain pass between S-charl and Lü.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Forest atmosphere and cultural landscape give it substantial discovery value, particularly in autumn, even though it lacks the raw spectacle of the higher tiers.

coverImage.alt: Documentary photograph of Bergtocht van S-charl naar Alp Sesvenna. 10-09-2019. (actm.) 24, representative of God da Tamangur: S-charl–Lü.

documents.name: Grande Dixence Ibex Trail
documents.summary: A compact high circuit above the Grande Dixence dam linking stark glacial terrain around Prafleuri with a high pass and imposing hydropower scenery.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The juxtaposition of giant engineering and austere high-alpine terrain is genuinely distinctive, although route spectacle is less sustained than the S/A glacier and pass traverses.

documents.name: Hoher Kasten–Saxer Lücke–Brülisau
documents.summary: A full Alpstein traverse from Hoher Kasten past Staubern and the Kreuzberge/Saxer Lücke walls, then down by Fählensee and Sämtisersee to Brülisau.
documents.whyWorthwhile: It turns the famous Saxer Lücke rock wall into a complete landscape journey, though the long descent and overlap with other Alpstein scenery keep it below A tier.

coverImage.alt: Documentary photograph of Hoher Kasten Gipfel, representative of Hoher Kasten–Saxer Lücke–Brülisau.

documents.name: Lavaux vineyard terraces: St-Saphorin–Lutry
documents.summary: A point-to-point walk through the UNESCO vineyard terraces of Lavaux above Lake Geneva with Alpine views beyond.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Historic terraced viticulture, lake scale and rail-to-rail logistics make this a genuinely distinctive lower-altitude Swiss hike rather than a fallback walk.

coverImage.alt: Documentary photograph of 2012-08-12 09-48-16 Switzerland Canton de Vaud Saint Saphorin, representative of Lavaux vineyard terraces: St-Saphorin–Lutry.

documents.name: Lugano
documents.summary: A compact Swiss-Italian lake city whose waterfront, elegant centre and cultural layer make a consistently rewarding Ticino stop.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The combination of lake scenery, walkability and Swiss-Italian urban character is clearly worthwhile for a Ticino itinerary without overstating Lugano as one of Switzerland's singular destination cities.

booking.note: No booking is required for the city identity.

coreExperience.note: Italian is local; the public-space experience is not language-dependent.
English and translation tools are practical for normal visitor needs.

mobility.note: The central lakefront and old centre are walkable; slopes increase effort away from the core.

legacy-effort-required.label: Effort required
legacy-effort-required.note: Low. Central Lugano is walkable and rail-connected; hillier areas are optional.

documents.name: Rhine Gorge, Caumasee and Conn loop
documents.summary: An accessible circuit combining pale Rhine Gorge landslide cliffs, turquoise water, forest and Caumasee.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Excellent lower-altitude scenery and logistics make it a strong regional hike, although it is less singular than the high geological routes in Sardona.

documents.name: Ritom–Cadagno–Tom lake circuit
documents.summary: A lake-rich circuit across the Piora plateau linking Ritom, biologically unusual meromictic Lake Cadagno and Lago di Tom.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The density of contrasting lakes and scientific interest make it a strong regional day, although the overall spectacle is less concentrated than Pizol or Murgseen.

documents.name: Swiss National Museum
documents.summary: A deep, centrally located survey of Swiss history and material culture that rewards several hours, especially for history-focused visitors.
documents.whyWorthwhile: It is a very good B-tier history museum and a worthwhile Zürich detour for the right audience, without inflating national significance into S/A experiential quality.

coreExperience.note: A multilingual digital layer including English is available.

digital.note: Official visitor information lists a multilingual museum app.

mobility.note: A complete visit spans a large museum complex and typically takes multiple hours.

legacy-booking-advice.label: Booking advice
legacy-booking-advice.note: Ordinary admission does not normally require advance booking.

legacy-accessibility-notes.label: Accessibility
legacy-accessibility-notes.note: Large museum visit; check current route details for specific mobility needs.

documents.name: Swiss Vapeur Parc
documents.summary: Swiss Vapeur Parc is a miniature railway destination in Le Bouveret, retained for distinctive visitor-experience quality.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A destination-scale ride-on miniature railway landscape with unusually elaborate infrastructure and strong younger-family appeal.

audience.notes: Editorial destination-fit profile derived from the researched positive age span. Bands without positive evidence remain unknown rather than being treated as a positive match or a hard prohibition. Individual rides and activities may have stricter operator rules.

documents.name: Trift Bridge from the road
documents.summary: The spectacular Trift glacial gorge and suspension bridge remain reachable in 2026 only with a substantially longer road-level approach because the Triftbahn is unavailable.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The bridge and retreating-glacier landscape remain exceptional, but 2026 access turns the standard high-reward outing into a long B-tier day.

documents.name: Val Frisal high-valley hike
documents.summary: A broad glacial headwater valley reached beyond the Scatlé primeval forest, with braided water, open meadow and a quiet high basin.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Unusually intact and peaceful, although the spectacle is subtler than the S/A high-alpine crossings.

documents.name: Valle di Lodano UNESCO forest circuit
documents.summary: An exceptionally strenuous circuit through the UNESCO-listed ancient beech forest of Valle di Lodano and abandoned high-alp landscape around Alpe Canaa.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The forest and cultural landscape are genuinely exceptional, but the enormous ascent lowers the effort-to-reward ratio for most travellers.

documents.name: ViaSbrinz: Guttannen–Obergesteln
documents.summary: A long historic mule-route crossing of the Grimsel through glacially polished granite, old transport infrastructure and modern hydropower landscapes.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The cultural and engineered landscape is excellent, but the very long day lowers broad effort-to-reward value.

documents.name: ViaStockalper: Simplon Dorf–Gondo
documents.summary: A short historic crossing through the Simplon corridor and Gondo gorge, where mule-route remnants sit beside several generations of trans-Alpine road engineering.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The human-history and gorge combination is unusually concentrated and provides cultural discovery value beyond pure alpine scenery.

documents.name: Walenpfad: Brunni–Bannalp
documents.summary: A sustained balcony trail linking Brunni and Bannalp high above Engelberg, enabled by mountain transport at both ends.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The route is consistently attractive and logistically clever, but its scenery is more substitutable than Switzerland’s strongest ridge and geological traverses.

documents.name: Aussichtspunkt Waid
documents.summary: A free, low-friction Zürich hillside viewpoint with a broad city, lake and Alpine panorama that consistently overdelivers for the effort.
documents.whyWorthwhile: As an easy urban panorama with repeated visitor praise, Waid clears C as a worthwhile nearby stop rather than a detour-generating excursion.

mobility.note: Bus access keeps the required walk short; walking from central Zürich is a longer optional approach.

documents.name: Grossmünster
documents.summary: Zürich's Reformation landmark remains rewarding for its Romanesque interior, modern stained glass and tower, but major restoration currently weakens its iconic exterior and panorama.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Even under restoration it is a worthwhile old-town stop for architecture and Reformation history, but the current restricted visual experience only clears C.

coreExperience.note: The building is primarily visual and historic.

audio.note: Multilingual audio support is listed for visitor discovery.

mobility.note: The church can be experienced without the tower; Karlsturm requires 187 steep narrow steps and has no lift.

current.note: The church remains visitable during the 2025-2029 restoration, but 2026 scaffolding affects the exterior and portions of the tower panorama.

documents.name: Reichenbach Falls
documents.summary: A high cascade above Meiringen reached by a historic funicular and linked to Sherlock Holmes lore.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A characterful natural-and-literary stop that is excellent when already in the Hasli valley.

documents.name: Sherlock Holmes Museum Meiringen
documents.summary: A tiny but unusually specific Sherlock Holmes pilgrimage built around a detailed Victorian reconstruction of Holmes and Watson's Baker Street sitting room.
documents.whyWorthwhile: For Sherlock Holmes enthusiasts already crossing the Bernese Oberland, the museum is a good specialist stop that clears C but not a major detour.

coreExperience.note: The reconstructed room is visual and current visitor evidence reports useful audio interpretation.
Audio interpretation makes the compact experience workable for English-speaking fans.

mobility.note: The museum is small; lower-level access details should be checked for mobility requirements.

legacy-booking-advice.label: Booking advice
legacy-booking-advice.note: General admission is low-friction; verify seasonal opening before a dedicated stop.

legacy-accessibility-notes.label: Accessibility
legacy-accessibility-notes.note: Small lower-level museum; complete step-free access was not independently verified.

documents.name: St. Beatus Caves
documents.summary: A developed show-cave complex above Lake Thun with an approximately kilometre-long visitor route.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A good cave stop for Lake Thun/Interlaken itineraries, but current comparison evidence does not support a major detour.

documents.name: Teufelsbrücke, Schöllenen
documents.summary: The historic Devil's Bridge crossing the narrow Schöllenen gorge on the old Gotthard route.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A compact but unusually atmospheric Gotthard-route stop combining landscape, engineering and history.

documents.name: Uetliberg Lookout Tower
documents.summary: A 178-step summit tower that upgrades Uetliberg's already strong view into an unobstructed 360-degree Zürich, lake and Alpine panorama.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The exact tower clears C because the incremental panorama is consistently enjoyable and distinctive at the summit, but it does not justify an independent detour.

mobility.note: There is an uphill summit approach from the rail stop and the tower itself has 178 steps.
